content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** The MSA gives Customer no convenience exit anywhere — Section 9 is limited to breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), Vendor security/SLA/legal/IP failures (9.3), and force majeure (27.3) — while Section 2.1 locks us into a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." That is walk-away territory under T4C and fails the fallback.

**Cure (preferred level, two surgical ops):**
1. New Section 9.4: 30-day convenience termination for Customer of the Agreement or any Order Form, plus an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
2. Conforming edit to 2.1: "without reduction rights, subject to Section 9.4" — preserving the no-reduction restriction while removing the contradiction with the new right.

The pro-rata prepaid-fee refund element is already met by Section 10.2 ("Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination"), so no refund language was added.
